description: SAP ERP audit log analysis context for the analysis (hunt) phase. Used by the LLM to identify suspicious patterns in SAP logs.

log_type_mapping.description: SM20 LOG = transaction started/table accessed (audit trail). CHANGE LOG = actual data modification with old/new values written via SAP's Change Document framework (CDHDR/CDPOS tables). Only CHANGE LOG entries with Old/New values prove actual data was modified. SM20 'Transaction Started' alone proves only that the user opened the transaction screen — not that they saved anything.

change_document_framework.description: SAP records data changes through the CDHDR/CDPOS framework. Every business object that supports change tracking has a 'Change Document Object' name (different from its table name). Understanding these names is essential for evaluating change records.

change_indicators.U: Update — existing field changed (will have Old val and New val)
change_indicators.E: Single field deletion within a record
change_indicators.J: Header insert (often paired with I records for line items)

auto_update_side_effects: BKPF.AEDAT and BKPF.UPDDT are automatically updated by the SAP kernel whenever any line item (BSEG) of a document is modified — these are NOT separate user actions
MARA.LAEDA / MARC.LAEDA auto-updates when material master fields change in any view
LFA1.ERDAT/AEDAT and KNA1.ERDAT/AEDAT auto-update when any sub-table (LFB1, LFBK, KNB1, KNVV) is modified
USR02.TRDAT (last login date) auto-updates on every login — this is not a security event
AGR_USERS.FROM_DAT/TO_DAT auto-update when role validity is recalculated, even without explicit user action

evidence_rules.transaction_started_only: A 'Transaction Started' event (SM20 audit log) does NOT prove data was modified. Only change records (CDPOS) with Table/Field/Old val/New val prove actual modifications.
evidence_rules.custom_tables: Any config transaction (SM30/SE16N) modifying tables starting with Z or Y is a custom configuration change — always report with the exact table name and field.
evidence_rules.master_vs_transactional: Changes to master data tables (LFA1, KNA1, MARA, USR02, ANLA) are higher severity than transactional data changes (BSEG, EKPO, VBAP). Report separately with different severities.
evidence_rules.auto_propagated_changes: If a CHANGE LOG shows BKPF.AEDAT, BKPF.UPDDT, MARA.LAEDA, LFA1.AEDAT, KNA1.AEDAT, or USR02.TRDAT changing — these are automatic kernel updates, NOT separate user actions. Do not count as additional findings unless the underlying object change is itself suspicious.
evidence_rules.change_indicator_meanings: I=Insert (new record), U=Update (field change with Old/New val), D=Delete (record deletion), E=Single field deletion. Treat I+U combos on the same key as the natural pattern for new-record creation.
evidence_rules.header_vs_line_changes: When BKPF (header) has only AEDAT/UPDDT changes but BSEG (lines) has substantive field changes (WRBTR, ZTERM, ZBD1P, etc.), the line items are the actual user action — the header changes are auto-updates. Quote the line item fields, not the header timestamps.
evidence_rules.cdhdr_cdpos_relationship: CDHDR is the change document header (one per save action). CDPOS contains the field-level changes. Multiple CDPOS entries for the same CDHDR_OBJECTID at the same timestamp = one save action with many fields, NOT a script.

failed_reason_codes.1: Authorization missing for transaction (general — could be overzealous role design or boundary testing)
failed_reason_codes.2: Transaction does not exist — typo (LOW risk; user fat-fingered a code that doesn't exist)
failed_reason_codes.3: Transaction is locked via SM01 (admin disabled it — user encounter is informational)
failed_reason_codes.4: Transaction not found in user menu (cosmetic, not a security event)
failed_reason_codes.5: Transaction does not start (program error or runtime issue, not a security event)
failed_reason_codes.6: No authorization (actual auth check failed — HIGH risk indicator of privilege boundary testing if repeated)
failed_reason_codes.7: Authorization buffer error (technical, retry usually succeeds — LOW risk)
failed_reason_codes.9: Cancelled by user (user pressed F12 or back — informational)
failed_reason_codes.A: Authorization check via S_TCODE failed (similar to 6 but for the tcode-level check specifically)

procure_to_pay_create.description: Full P2P fraud lifecycle — vendor master modification combined with PO creation/modification in same session by same actor
indicators: Vendor master change (XK02/FK02/BP/MASS) + PO action (ME21N/ME22N) in same session
watch_for: LFBK changes specifically — vendor bank routing

procure_to_pay_full.description: Vendor + PO + Goods Receipt + Invoice + Payment all in one session by one actor
indicators: XK02 + ME21N + MIGO + MIRO + F-58 within same session, or any 3+ of these combinations

order_to_cash.description: Full O2C fraud lifecycle — credit limit modification, sales order, delivery, billing in same session
indicators: FD32 (credit) + VA01/VA02 + VL01N/VL02N + VF01 in same session

user_provisioning_self_grant.description: User creates/modifies a user account and grants themselves or a related account elevated roles
indicators: SU01 changes + PFCG role assignment + login as the new user, all within session

journal_entry_then_clear.description: Manual journal entry posted, then immediately cleared by same user (covers tracks)
indicators: FB01/FB50 + F-03/FB1S in same session targeting same documents

asset_create_then_dispose.description: Asset created and disposed within short window, possibly with retirement to write-off
indicators: AS01 + ABAVN/ABAON + F-90/F-92 within session

config_change_during_close.description: G/L account, tax config, or posting period config changed during financial close
indicators: OB52 + FS00/SA39 + FB01 in window of fiscal close (last business day of month/quarter/year)

payroll_data_self_modification.description: User modifies their own HR records and triggers payroll
indicators: PA30 on own personnel number + PA03/PAUX in same session

transport_bypass_production.description: Direct table edit in production via SE16N &SAP_EDIT or SM30 without transport request
indicators: SE16N with &SAP_EDIT flag
SM30 modifications without TR number captured
SE38 program execution writing to tables
transport_bypass_production.severity: CRITICAL — bypasses entire SAP change management

po_quantity_or_price_inflation.description: Purchase order line/schedule quantity or unit price increased after creation — direct procurement fraud lever
indicators: EKPO.MENGE [U] new>old (especially ≥2x or >100 unit absolute increase) via ME22N/ME23N or SE16(N)
EKET.MENGE [U] new>old in same window
EKPO.NETPR / EKPO.NETWR / EKPO.BRTWR [U] increased — particularly with currency switch (e.g. EUR→USD)
EKPO.PEINH or BPRME unit-base changes inflating line value silently
watch_for: Same actor doing ME22N/ME23N CDPOS write while requested_tcode=SE16
Subsequent MIGO 101 receipt at the inflated quantity
Subsequent MIRO/F-58 invoice and payment matching the inflated PO

delivery_then_reverse_GI.description: Delivery created (VL01N/VL02N) followed by reverse goods issue (VL09 or MB1A 262) without subsequent re-issue or operational explanation — silent inventory removal
indicators: VL01N delivery create → VL09 reverse GI on the same VBELN with no follow-on VL02N re-post within reasonable window
Mass VL09 events that are NOT followed by re-VL02N in 30 minutes
Same actor performs VL01N + VL09 against same VBELN
watch_for: LIPS.LFIMG quantity reduced after pick (LT0A confirm) — stock vanishes between confirmation and goods issue
LIPS.LGORT / LIPS.WERKS changed mid-delivery — diversion to off-warehouse storage

transfer_order_create_then_cancel.description: Mass transfer order create (LT01) and cancel (LT12/LT0K) in same session — paper trail erasure for inventory diversion
indicators: LT01 + LT12 in same session same actor
LT0A confirm of TO whose destination LGORT differs from baseline
Mass LT12 deletion with no audit-trail of why

phantom_stock_creation.description: Initial stock entry (movement type 561 via MB1C) creating inventory from nothing without procurement linkage
indicators: MB1C 561 movements posted by non-Basis-during-go-live actor
MB1A 562 reversing a 561 to mask the trail
MSEG entries for movement 561/562/501/502 outside documented inventory-load windows

shipment_cover_up.description: Shipment header deletion or status manipulation after delivery posting — cover-up of physical movement records
indicators: VT70 delete shipment after VL02N goods issue posted
VTTK manual status change to a finalized/locked state on the same actor
VTSP segment manipulation hiding stops

equipment_misappropriation.description: Equipment master ownership / location / status modified outside of a service order or PM workflow
indicators: EQUI.SERNR/EQUNR/EQTYP changed via IE02 without IW32 maintenance order context
EQUI plant/location change to different cost-bearing org
EQUZ status change to scrapped/idle that doesn't match maintenance plan

handling_unit_repack_to_mask_quantity.description: Handling unit content re-packed (item moved between HUs) without supporting transfer order — common cover-up for partial diversion
indicators: VEKP / VEPO modifications via HU02 with quantity rebalancing across HUs
HUMSEG entries with material/quantity reassignment without LTAK reference

billing_cancellation_at_scale.description: Mass cancellation of billing documents (VF11) — revenue manipulation or unauthorized credit issuance
indicators: ≥10 VF11 in one session by same actor with no VF01/VF02 re-bill follow-up
VBRK/VBRP cancellation without service or quality notification linkage

ob52_then_backdated_post.description: Posting period reopen via OB52 followed by backdated FI document posting in the reopened period
indicators: OB52 modification of T001B period control
FB01/FB50/FB02 with BUDAT in the reopened period within 24 hours of the OB52 change
Reversal (FB08/FBR2) targeting documents in the reopened period

se37_rfc_read_table_extract.description: SE37 invocation of RFC_READ_TABLE / BBP_RFC_READ_TABLE / RFC_GET_TABLE_ENTRIES with high ROWCOUNT, especially against AGR_*, USR0*, PA0*, BSEG, LFBK — direct bulk extract via function module
indicators: SE37 + function module RFC_READ_TABLE / BBP_RFC_READ_TABLE / RFC_GET_TABLE_ENTRIES
ROWCOUNT parameter set to a large value (>10000)
OPTIONS filter referencing sensitive table by name (AGR_USERS, USR02, PA0008, PA0009, LFBK, KNBK)

custom_z_program_data_export.description: Custom (Z*/Y*) program executed via SE38/SA38 reading sensitive tables, often with RFC_READ_TABLE inside, sometimes named ZRFC_DOWNLOAD / Z*_EXPORT / Z*_EXTRACT
indicators: SE38 / SA38 execution of Z*/Y* program whose name contains DOWNLOAD/EXPORT/EXTRACT/DUMP
Z program execution that calls RFC_READ_TABLE on AGR_USERS / USR02 / PA0* / BSEG / LFBK

debugger_protected_field_change.description: ABAP debugger (/h) used to bypass screen authority and change a protected field directly in memory before save
indicators: Successful SE38/SE80 followed by /h debug entry on a transaction touching high-tier fields (WRBTR, MENGE, BANKL, BANKN, IBAN, ZLSCH, ZBFIX, USR02.UFLAG, AGR_USERS.AGR_NAME)
Same actor + immediate CDPOS write on tier_high field via tcode that normally requires workflow approval

audit_disable_then_modify.description: RSAU_CONFIG / SM19 audit configuration changed (or DBTABLOG modified) followed by financial / privilege changes by same actor — audit suppression preceding the act
indicators: RSAU_CONFIG / SM19 modification by non-Basis-Audit actor
DBTABLOG configuration change
Followed within window by FB01/FBV0/PFCG/SU01/MIRO by same actor

sicf_then_external_egress.description: SICF/SOAMANAGER service activated/created in production followed by data-bearing transactions or RFC calls — external HTTP egress preparation
indicators: SICF service activation in PRD by non-Basis actor
SOAMANAGER endpoint registration
STRUST certificate import
SM59 RFC destination create pointing to external host

tcode_deviation_with_high_tier_change.description: Firefighter session has Tcode Deviation = YES (approved tcode != actual tcode) AND a high-tier-field change is recorded — actual activity exceeded the approved scope
indicators: Requested Tcode != Transaction Code (SAP GRC tcode-deviation flag)
And concurrent CDPOS [U/I/D] on tier_high field per field_type_awareness.control_fields_high_risk

data_scraping_description: 15+ direct reads of the same sensitive table via SE16/SE16N/SE16H in one session indicates data scraping. Master data tables (KNA1, LFA1, USR02, MARA) are higher-risk targets. Read-only access (activity 03) on configuration tables is reconnaissance, not modification.

system_user_types.DIALOG: Normal interactive user — should generate user-driven SM20 events with terminal info
system_user_types.SYSTEM: Background/RFC user — programmatic access, no terminal expected (e.g. WF-BATCH, ALEREMOTE)
system_user_types.COMMUNICATION: RFC-only user, cannot do dialog logon (e.g. CPIC users)
system_user_types.SERVICE: Anonymous service user (e.g. internet-facing apps) — should never have wide auth
system_user_types.REFERENCE: Template user, should never log in directly
system_user_types.rules: DIALOG users doing what looks like SYSTEM activity (millisecond gaps, batch programs) usually means a script — see if it correlates to an authorized job (SM37). SYSTEM users doing DIALOG-like activity (interactive transactions like SU01, SE16N) is suspicious — investigate.

field_type_awareness.rules: WRBTR/DMBTR/DMBE2 are CURRENCY amounts. BRGEW/NTGEW/VOLUM are PHYSICAL weights/volumes — never describe physical-field changes as 'financial loss'. IDENTITY_GUID is a system linkage GUID, NOT a credential or password hash. Date fields auto-update (AEDAT, ERDAT, TRDAT) on related actions and are usually side-effects. Control fields (ZBD1P, ZTERM, ZLSCH, MWSKZ, MANSP, EMPFK, LNRZA, BANKL/BANKN) are HIGHEST-RISK because they govern WHEN/HOW/WHERE money flows — changes to these fields warrant scrutiny regardless of the transaction used.

tcode_behavior_facts.description: Important behaviors of standard SAP transactions that affect interpretation. SAP help and forums confirm these as standard features, not exploits.

facts.FBL5N_FBL3N_FBL1N: Despite being called 'display' transactions, FBL5N (customer line items), FBL3N (G/L line items), and FBL1N (vendor line items) all expose the menu path 'Environment → Document → Change' and a 'Mass Change' button (Ctrl+Shift+F9). Mass Change calls function module MASS_CHANGE_FI to update payment terms, dunning data, payment methods, text, and assignment fields across selected line items. Change records on BSEG/BKPF originating from FBL3N/FBL5N/FBL1N are STANDARD AR/AP clerk activity, NOT BAdI/exit exploits.
facts.FB02: Document change. Limited to fields permitted by the document-change rules table T030U. Cannot change posted amounts — only ancillary fields (ZTERM, payment block, text). Multiple BSEG line changes from one FB02 save = one user action.
facts.MASS: Generic mass-maintenance transaction. Available for material master, customer master, vendor master, sales order, purchase order, etc. High-volume legitimate change source.
facts.MM17_BMBC: Material mass maintenance. Hundreds of MARA/MARC changes per save is normal.
facts.F.13_F-32_F-44: Automatic clearing programs. Generate large numbers of clearing assignments (AUGBL on BSEG records) per run. Hundreds of clearings at the same timestamp from a single F.13 run is standard.
facts.FBRA: Reset cleared items (mass clearing reversal). Designed for fixing botched payment runs or bank statement imports. Volume often equals the original F110 run's document count.
facts.F110: Automated payment program. Produces large volumes of REGUH/REGUP entries and BSEG clearings. A failed F110 run is the most common cause of subsequent FBRA mass reversals.
facts.F.05_FAGL_FC_VAL: Foreign currency revaluation. Period-end batch program that revalues open items at month-end exchange rates. Generates large numbers of journal entries to revaluation accounts. Standard month-end activity.
facts.AFAB: Asset depreciation run. Generates one document per asset per period. Runs once per period (monthly). Produces hundreds to thousands of postings — all expected.
facts.AJAB_AJRW: Year-end asset closing and balance carryforward. Once-a-year mass operations affecting all assets — entirely expected.
facts.RFFOEDI1_RFFOUS_T_RFFOAVIS: Standard payment medium programs. Run as part of F110 to produce bank files.
facts.SE16N_with_SAP_EDIT: Setting the user parameter '&SAP_EDIT' switches SE16N from read-only to edit mode. ANY use of this parameter on production is a transport-bypass policy violation regardless of intent.
facts.SHDB_SM35: Batch input recording and processing. Recordings replay user actions — often used legitimately for data migration. The recording session itself produces a flood of CHG records at machine speed; this is the design, not automation abuse.
facts.VL09: Reverse goods issue. Used legitimately to correct wrong goods issues (then immediately re-VL02N). High counts of VL09 with NO subsequent VL02N re-post on the same VBELN within ~30 minutes is a silent-inventory-removal red flag.
facts.VL02N: Change outbound delivery — covers picking, packing, post goods issue. Legitimate uses include LGORT change for staging. LGORT switches from a tracked location to a non-tracked one mid-pick is suspicious.
facts.LT0A: Confirm transfer order (pick confirmation). Should match the planned LTAP quantities (WMENG vs VFMNG). Material/quantity divergences at confirmation are suspicious.
facts.LT12: Cancel transfer order. Mass LT12 in same session is a paper-trail erasure pattern — investigate WHICH TOs were cancelled and whether stock movements happened anyway.
facts.MB1A_262: Reverse goods issue movement. 262 reverses 261. Legitimate when paired with a wrong-quantity correction; suspicious when not paired.
facts.MB1C_561: Initial entry of stock balance. Creates inventory FROM NOTHING — only valid during system go-live or documented inventory loads. Outside those windows it is phantom-stock creation.
facts.VT70: Delete shipment. Should NEVER delete a shipment whose VBELN-LIPS link was already active (i.e., GI posted) — that is shipment cover-up.
facts.SE37_RFC_READ_TABLE: Direct invocation of RFC_READ_TABLE function module via SE37 lets an actor bulk-extract any table the actor has read on. ROWCOUNT > 10000 against AGR_USERS / USR02 / PA0008 / PA0009 / LFBK / KNBK / BSEG is direct exfil — not a developer test.
facts.OB52_period_control: Open posting periods. Legitimate at month-end close coordination — but reopening a closed period followed by FB01/FB50/FB02 backdated postings within 24 hours is bypass of period control.
facts.Custom_namespace_tcodes: Tcodes inside customer namespace (/<NAMESPACE>/<NAME> e.g. /MVNT/ADMIN, /SAPSII/*) are vendor or customer-built. They are unaudited unless explicitly registered in the audit framework. Treat repeated custom-namespace tcode usage by a firefighter session as 'requires manual review'.
facts.VF11_billing_cancellation: Cancel billing document. Legitimate corrections occur in pairs (VF11 + new VF01). ≥10 VF11 with no follow-on VF01 in same session is revenue manipulation.
facts.Tcode_Deviation_flag: When the audit log's Tcode Deviation column is YES (Requested Tcode != Transaction Code), the firefighter executed something OUTSIDE the approved scope. Combined with any high-tier field change, this is a hard policy violation regardless of business intent — score floor 70.

ticket_scope_table_mapping.description: Maps ticket intent keywords to the SAP tables they legitimately cover. Used by the challenger to deterministically verify scope alignment instead of letting the LLM guess.

legitimate_high_volume_patterns.description: Operations that LEGITIMATELY produce thousands of change records per session/run. Do not flag volume alone as suspicious for these.

patterns.expected_volume: 1 BSEG clearing per open invoice paid + 1 REGUH per payment + 1 REGUP per item
patterns.frequency: weekly to daily depending on company size

patterns.expected_volume: 1 AUGBL set per cleared invoice (often thousands per run)
1 ANLC + 1 BKPF/BSEG per asset per depreciation area per period
1 revaluation entry per open item in foreign currency (thousands typical)
all assets carried to new fiscal year
1 MARA/MARC change per material × fields changed
as recorded — can be thousands at machine speed
patterns.frequency: ad-hoc, usually data migration or mass corrections

patterns.trigger: FBRA mass reversal of failed F110
patterns.expected_volume: matches the failed F110's document count

compliance_event_calendar.description: Known regulatory events that cause mass legitimate changes to specific SAP data. When changes match these patterns, presume compliance/maintenance — not fraud.

events.name: SEPA Migration
events.note: Mass conversion of BBAN to IBAN across vendor/customer bank details

events.name: EUR Currency Migration
events.note: Mass conversion of legacy currencies to EUR

events.name: Bank merger SWIFT changes (general)
events.note: Bank acquisitions and rebrandings periodically force mass SWIFT updates — apply ALL records of same bank, never targeting specific vendors

events.name: GST/VAT rate changes
events.note: Government rate changes force mass tax-config updates

events.name: IFRS-16 Lease accounting transition
events.note: Mass asset reclassifications when adopting new lease standard

events.name: Withholding tax legislative changes
events.note: Tax authority changes force mass withholding configuration

authorization_objects.description: Key SAP authorization objects and the activity values that determine read vs write access. Use to determine the actual capability granted.

objects.S_TCODE: Transaction-level access (does user have FBL5N at all?)
objects.F_BKPF_BUK: FI document — company code level. Activity 03=display, 01=create, 02=change
objects.F_LFA1_GRP: Vendor account group — controls who can create new vendors
objects.S_TABU_DIS: Generic table maintenance via SM30. Activity 02=write, 03=display
objects.S_DEVELOP: ABAP development — Object types DEBUG, EDITOR, CLAS, FUGR, PROG, TABL
objects.S_USER_GRP: User maintenance per user group. Activity 01=create, 02=change, 06=delete

authorization_objects.rule: Activity 03 = read only. Activity 01/02/06 = write/modify. SE16N entries with activity 03 are reconnaissance/policy deviation, NEVER 'data manipulation'.

document_types.description: Standard SAP FI document types. The first 2 characters reveal the source.
document_types.rule: SA documents posted via FB01 to recently-created G/L accounts with vague text by the same user who created the accounts is a HIGH-RISK signal. SU reversals on the user's own KZ payments deserves scrutiny.

usecase_mapping._doc: Maps SAP entities (tcode classes / table classes / toxic combos / finding types) to one of the three customer-facing use cases. Used by usecase_classifier.py to tag findings post-challenger. A finding may carry multiple UC tags; classifier picks the highest-priority one as primary.

financial_fraud.name: Financial Fraud
financial_fraud.description: Vendor self-dealing, posting-period manipulation, GL/master tampering, authorization escalation enabling fraud, code injection enabling fraud, purchasing fraud, payment manipulation

logistic_fraud.name: Logistic Fraud
logistic_fraud.description: Delivery manipulation, goods-issue reversals, inventory theft via transfer orders, shipment diversion/deletion, equipment misappropriation, handling-unit fraud, phantom stock, billing-side cancellations affecting revenue recognition

data_exfiltration.name: Data Exfiltration
data_exfiltration.description: Mass data downloads, sensitive table reads outside FF scope, RFC-based extraction, debugger abuse, external HTTP egress, custom export tools, session anomalies revealing impersonation

other.name: Other / Operational
other.description: Findings that do not cleanly map to financial/logistic/exfil — typically informational, system-maintenance noise, or compliance-required disclosures

rules: If a finding's tcode is in financial_fraud.tcode_classes AND the modified field is in field_type_awareness.control_fields_high_risk AND the field is a money/payment field (WRBTR, DMBTR, NETPR, NETWR, BRTWR, KBETR, BANKL, BANKN, IBAN, ZLSCH, ZBFIX, EMPFG), classify as financial_fraud — even if other UCs would also match.
If a finding shows direct table read at scale (≥15 reads or RFC_READ_TABLE / Z*_DOWNLOAD pattern) regardless of target UC, classify as data_exfiltration.

If a finding involves delivery (LIKP/LIPS/VBPA), transfer order (LTAK/LTAP), handling unit (VEKP/VEPO), shipment (VTTK/VTTP), equipment (EQUI/EQUZ), or movement type (BWART) without a financial-doc lever, classify as logistic_fraud.

If a finding is a tcode-deviation (Tcode Deviation = YES) on a high-tier-field change, tag the primary UC by the tcode/table touched AND additionally tag with 'data_exfiltration' as a scope_compliance signal.
If a finding cannot be unambiguously mapped, classify as other and let synthesis decide whether to surface it.

firefighter_scope_compliance._doc: Rules for evaluating whether a firefighter session stayed within its approved scope. Drives scope_compliance findings + downstream UC tagging.

tcode_deviation_rule.description: When the audit log column 'Tcode Deviation' is YES, the actual transaction code differs from what the firefighter was approved for. This is a HARD signal of scope creep regardless of business intent.

scoring.deviation_with_no_change: INFO — possibly an exploration that didn't save
scoring.deviation_at_volume: If >50% of the session is deviated, baseline severity is HIGH for the entire session

developer_ffid_rule.description: FFID names containing DEV/ABAP/TECH/ADMIN/IT/BASIS suggest developer or technical firefighter — these accounts have inherently broader risk surface (debugger access, code editor authority).
developer_ffid_rule.rule: Developer FFIDs should ONLY be used for development-system or break-fix code work. Use against productive transactional/master data (FB01, ME21N, XK02, VL01N) is automatic scope violation regardless of approval status.

approved_tcode_categorization.description: When the requested/approved tcode differs in CLASS from the actual tcode, the deviation is more severe than a same-class deviation.
examples: approved=SE16 (query class) but actual=ME22N (purchasing) → cross-class deviation = HIGH
approved=SE16 but actual=PFCG (security class) → cross-class = CRITICAL
approved=ME21N but actual=ME22N → same purchasing class = LOW (still deviation but lower severity)

custom_namespace_rule.description: Custom-namespace tcodes (/<NAMESPACE>/<NAME> e.g. /MVNT/ADMIN, /SAPSII/*, /1BCDWB/*) are vendor or customer-built and may not have CDPOS wiring, making them unauditable by default.
custom_namespace_rule.rule: Repeated custom-namespace tcode usage by a firefighter session = 'requires manual review' at minimum HIGH severity unless the customer's audit framework explicitly registers them.

code_execution_patterns._doc: Patterns for detecting privileged code execution that bypasses normal screen/auth controls.

se37_function_module_direct.description: Direct invocation of a function module via SE37 — bypasses any tcode-level auth check on the underlying transaction
indicators: SE37 in TRANSACTION CODE column
Function module names like RFC_READ_TABLE, BBP_RFC_READ_TABLE, RFC_GET_TABLE_ENTRIES, BAPI_*_CHANGE, BAPI_*_CREATE on master data

se24_class_direct.description: Direct execution of a class method via SE24 — same bypass profile as SE37 for OO code
indicators: SE24 in TRANSACTION CODE column
Class methods invoked directly

se38_z_program_export.description: Custom Z*/Y* program executed via SE38/SA38 that reads sensitive tables — often named ZRFC_DOWNLOAD, Z*_EXPORT, Z*_EXTRACT, Z*_DUMP
indicators: SE38/SA38 invoking Z program with DOWNLOAD/EXPORT/EXTRACT/DUMP in name
Program references RFC_READ_TABLE on AGR_USERS/USR02/PA0*/BSEG/LFBK/KNBK

abap_debugger_field_change.description: ABAP debugger (/h) used to bypass screen authority and modify a protected field in memory before save
indicators: DEBUG keyword in details / event_class
/h or transaction-debug entry pattern
Subsequent CDPOS write on tier_high field via tcode that normally requires workflow

rfc_read_table_bulk.description: RFC_READ_TABLE call (via SE37 or programmatic) with high ROWCOUNT against sensitive tables
indicators: ROWCOUNT > 10000
OPTIONS filter referencing AGR_USERS/USR0*/PA0*/BSEG/LFBK/KNBK/PAYR
